description: The Scarlet Containment is a sphere of pure antimatter roughly ninety-four kilometers across, held in place by a natural magnetic field that has persisted for over two billion years. Its boundary glows with a faint, angry scarlet produced by the constant micro-annihilation of stray hydrogen atoms and dust particles that drift into contact with its surface. These tiny detonations create a perpetual halo of light and radiation that marks the pocket as one of the most visible and most dangerous objects in the sector.

The pocket is remarkably well-behaved for something capable of destroying a star system. Its natural containment field holds with a stability that baffles physicists, maintaining a near-perfect spherical boundary that has not measurably fluctuated in the decades since its discovery. The primary danger comes not from the pocket itself but from the intense radiation environment it creates and the catastrophic consequences of any interaction with its surface. Even a small ship impacting the pocket would release enough energy to rival a nuclear detonation.

The Scarlet Containment was discovered in 2461 by a long-range survey drone that detected its unmistakable gamma signature from over forty million kilometers away. Initial excitement over the largest known antimatter deposit quickly gave way to sobering calculations about the consequences of its destabilization. The pocket contains enough antimatter to power human civilization for millennia, but it also contains enough to end it. This tension between extraordinary promise and existential risk has defined every interaction with the anomaly since its discovery.

A permanent monitoring station orbits at a distance of five thousand kilometers, crewed by rotating teams of physicists and hazard specialists who study the containment field and track the pocket's status. The Galactic Energy Consortium continues to lobby aggressively for extraction rights, arguing that advancing containment technology makes safe harvesting feasible. Critics counter that no technology can guarantee safety when the consequences of failure are measured in stellar sterilization. For now, the Scarlet Containment sits in its ancient magnetic cradle, patient and lethal, a treasure chest that might also be a bomb.
